name: Legs B — single leg & eccentric
summary: Single-leg strength and slow eccentrics — the Down-Run-specific session. Same session every time; weights climb by double progression as each exercise reaches the top of its rep range on every set.
equipment: Dumbbells, bench, trap (hex) bar, a 20–30 cm box or step.
when_to_use: Second leg session of the week, on a quality-run day at least 6 hours after the run. Not the day before a long run.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
cues: Rear foot on a bench, front foot far enough forward that the knee stays over the mid-foot
Lower straight down for 2–3 s, torso slightly forward
Drive through the front heel; finish all reps on one leg, then switch
exercises.why: Single-leg strength exposes and fixes left/right differences — every running stride is single-leg.

exercises.name: Trap-bar deadlift
cues: Stand in the centre, hips down, chest up, grip the handles
Push the floor away; hips and shoulders rise together
Lower under control; reset each rep
exercises.why: Heavy whole-leg strength with less back stress than a straight bar.

exercises.name: Eccentric step-down
cues: Stand on a box on one leg; lower the other heel to the floor over 3–4 s
Knee tracks over the second toe, hips level
Tap and come back up; start at bodyweight, add a dumbbell when easy
exercises.why: Slow lowering under load is exactly what downhill running does to the quads — this is the most Comrades-specific lift.

exercises.name: Calf raise, straight knee
cues: Full stretch at the bottom, high rise, 3 s down
exercises.why: Calf and ankle strength for the long run and the ankle niggle.
